messages.text: Alonso to race in formidable Dakar Rally with Aston Martin

metadata.summary: Fernando Alonso will race in the Dakar Rally for Aston Martin in January.
metadata.content: Fernando Alonso: Aston Martin driver to race in Dakar Rally ahead of 2027 F1 season in return to rally-raid event | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Fernando Alonso: Aston Martin driver to race in Dakar Rally ahead of 2027 F1 season in return to rally-raid event Aston Martin's F1 driver joins the marque's first foray into the hugely-challenging Dakar Rally in January; 2027 event being held in Portugal and Morocco; watch the Las Vegas GP this weekend on Sky Sports F1, with qualifying at 4am on Saturday and the race at 4am on Sunday Tuesday 17 November 2026 08:31, UK Image: Fernando Alonso back behind the wheel of a rally-raid car Fernando Alonso will race in the Dakar Rally for Aston Martin in January. The 45-year-old will return to compete in the legendary off-road endurance event seven years on from his one previous appearance, when he finished 13th with Toyota. That came during Alonso's two-year stint out of Formula 1 but this time he will race in Dakar ahead of what will be a record-extending 24th campaign in the sport after he extended his deal with Aston Martin's F1 team for the 2027 season. Local media reports in Reeves' hometown of Limerick ​said he underwent surgery ‌after his knockout loss to Gary Cully in ​a junior welterweight bout in August in Dublin and had been in a ​medically induced coma since. "Everyone at Queensberry is devastated to learn ‌of the passing of Lee Reeves," the promoters said in a statement. "Lee was an immensely talented boxer, as well ⁠as a true role model ​and inspiration to his community." Cully ​described Reeves as "a character and ​a gent". messages.text: Ravens' season on the brink after loss to struggling Chargers

metadata.summary: Justin Herbert and Omarion Hampton ran for first-half touchdowns as the Los Angeles Chargers earned their first win of the season, manhandling Baltimore at the line of scrimmage in a 23-20 victory over the Ravens on Monday night.
metadata.content: NFL: Baltimore Ravens beaten by Los Angeles Chargers to leave season on brink as Justin Herbert's side claim first win | NFL News | Sky Sports Skip to main content NFL: Baltimore Ravens beaten by Los Angeles Chargers to leave season on brink as Justin Herbert's side claim first win The Los Angeles Chargers end their losing 0-8 start to the season by beating the Baltimore Ravens 23-20 behind Omarion Hampton's impressive efforts on the ground; the Ravens remain without quarterback Lamar Jackson, who is out for up to 10 weeks with a thumb injury Tuesday 17 November 2026 06:36, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Los Angeles Chargers against Baltimore Ravens from Week 10 of the NFL season Justin Herbert and Omarion Hampton ran for first-half touchdowns as the Los Angeles Chargers earned their first win of the season, manhandling Baltimore at the line of scrimmage in a 23-20 victory over the Ravens on Monday night. Derrick Henry was held to 10 yards on 10 carries, although he did score two touchdowns as Baltimore (4-6) skidded to its fifth straight loss and by far the most demoralising. The Chargers (1-8) had lost 11 in a row dating back to last season but they outrushed the Ravens 160-16. The combined 15 straight losses by the Chargers and Ravens entering the game was a record for a Monday night game. metadata.content: McLaren chief Zak Brown says advice from Novak Djokovic will help F1 team bounce back from losing titles to Mercedes | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Exclusive McLaren chief Zak Brown says advice from Novak Djokovic will help F1 team bounce back from losing titles to Mercedes Listen to Sky Sports' full length interview with McLaren chief Zak Brown on the latest episode of The F1 Show; watch the Las Vegas GP this weekend on Sky Sports F1, with qualifying at 4am on Saturday and the race at 4am on Sunday Tuesday 17 November 2026 06:10, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking on the Sky Sports F1 Show podcast, Zak Brown shares a hilarious response to Mercedes sealing the 2026 championship double McLaren chief executive Zak Brown says he is using advice from Novak Djokovic to aid his team's attempt to bounce back after losing both of their Formula 1 titles to Mercedes this season. Lando Norris was replaced as world champion by Kimi Antonelli at the Mexico City Grand Prix earlier this month before Mercedes sealed a dominant Constructors' Championship triumph a week later in Brazil. McLaren won their first constructors' title in 26 years in 2024 before repeating the feat the following year, but a major change in the sport's regulations reset the pecking order ahead of the 2026 season. messages.text: British doubles No 1 criticises ATP bosses at trophy presentation absence

metadata.summary: British doubles No 1 Henry Patten has taken a swipe at ATP bosses for their absence from a trophy presentation in Turin on Monday.
metadata.content: Henry Patten: British doubles No 1 takes swipe at ATP chairman and CEO for absence from trophy presentation | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Henry Patten: British doubles No 1 takes swipe at ATP chairman and CEO for absence from trophy presentation Henry Patten uses trophy presentation to focus on the absence of ATP bosses, reigniting his opposition to the doubles reform expected for 2028; You can watch the ATP Finals in Turin this week on Sky Sports Tennis Monday 16 November 2026 20:40, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player British doubles star Henry Patten hit out at ATP chairman Andrea Gaudenzi and CEO Eno Polo for missing his world No 1 trophy presentation British doubles No 1 Henry Patten has taken a swipe at ATP bosses for their absence from a trophy presentation in Turin on Monday. Upon receiving the year-end doubles No 1 trophy from chief tour officer Andre Silva, alongside his Finnish partner Harri Heliovaara, Patten called out the ATP chairman Andrea Gaudenzi and CEO Eno Polo. "For us, it's a really big deal. It's a real shame that the ATP chairman and CEO don't think the same." Patten said.
